evidence: Source: task/environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template rules/projects/webdev-task-template/environment/Dockerfile (diff empty; sha256 0a75419e...67d1). It has 'FROM node:22-bookworm-slim' (tagged base, no 'latest'), 'ENV NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules', 'RUN npm install -g --no-audit --no-fund express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1', 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/', 'COPY assets/ /assets/', 'RUN chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets && mkdir -p /app && git -C /app init ... commit -m "Initialize task workspace"', WORKDIR /app, CMD sleep infinity; no COPY of solution/ or tests/. These match exactly what quality-checks.md #15 requires. The golden's only npm deps (solution/app/package.json: express 5.1.0, better-sqlite3 12.4.1; server.js:10-11 requires) are the pre-installed ones, and solve.sh only copies files (no npm install). Public brief integration.md:3 tells the model 'Express and better-sqlite3 are already installed globally and found through NODE_PATH', instruction.md:5 points at /assets/seed_data.json and /instructions, which the image stages. task.toml [environment] has no docker_image (the Dockerfile is not shadowed). tests/Dockerfile installs the same express@5.1.0/better-sqlite3@12.4.1 with NODE_PATH, and test.sh:106,162 passes the same NODE_PATH, so the declared world is the same at grade time. Runtime evidence from me, 9 Oct 2026: I built a fresh copy of the frozen environment/ directory as the uniquely tagged qc-r3-row15-kittle-agent:tmp. The build succeeded, and I removed the image afterwards. The scripted golden's cw-editor-agent-r3 image is not provably built from these bytes, so I did not rely on it. Results from 'docker run --network none --user 65534:65534': node v22.23.2; NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules; require resolved express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1, and better-sqlite3 opened :memory: (sqlite 3.50.4), so the native addon loads offline as nobody; /assets/seed_data.json (5701 bytes, same sha256 f69616e2... as solution seed) and the three /instructions/*.md files are present and world-readable (r-x from chmod a+rX); /app contains only .git and an empty .gitkeep. I also ran the frozen solve.sh offline in the image (--network none) and copied /app aside. The app ran as uid 65534 with env -i PATH/NODE_PATH/HOME/PORT/DB_PATH and cwd /tmp: no /app/node_modules was created, /api/health returned 200, / returned 200, and the DB was created with tables matters/messages/users/walls/versions/... So no run-time install is needed. Notes (not defects, template-controlled per AGENTS.md, so they cannot be changed task-locally): the base is tag-pinned, not digest-pinned (node:22 floats patch releases; locally it resolves to node@sha256:83f487e0...); apt packages are unpinned (the workbook's check-dockerfiles.py treats this as a NOTE); /app is 'empty' apart from the template's .gitkeep/.git commit, which is the template's intended git-initialised workspace. Counterexample probes: (a) A broken app that could pass would be one needing an extra npm package (e.g. ws) that the agent installs into /app/node_modules during its public-network phase. That is outside this row: it concerns the submission and verifier (rows 19/22 and the test.sh symlink policy), not whether the agent image builds the declared world. (b) A conforming alternative that could fail would be one using only express plus better-sqlite3 as the brief says. Both resolve offline as uid 65534 in the measured image, so I found no conforming alternative that this image would break.
